claims.text: ALBIREO is a detector-agnostic framework that skips detector invocation based on scene content and object state.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO is a detector-agnostic framework that skips detector invocation based on scene content and object state.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: We present ALBIREO, a detector-agnostic, codec-free, adaptive inference framework that wraps off-the-shelf object detectors and decides when detector invocation can be safely skipped based on scene content and per-object temporal state.
claims.reason: Section I explicitly describes ALBIREO as detector-agnostic and skipping based on scene content and object state.

claims.text: ALBIREO improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6% on Thor.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6% on Thor.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On the primary YOLO26x configuration, ALBIREO improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6% on Thor.
claims.reason: Section IV-B and Table III confirm the +0.8 pp AP@50 improvement and 17.6% energy reduction on Thor for YOLO26x.

claims.text: Edge video object detection is costly due to per-frame detector invocation, drawing 70 W on Jetson AGX Thor.
claims.poster_quote: Edge video object detection is costly due to per-frame detector invocation, drawing 70 W on Jetson AGX Thor.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Running YOLO26x on every frame draws 70 W of total board power on Jetson AGX Thor (Blackwell, 130 W TDP), of which 34 W (49%) is the GPU power.
claims.reason: Section I and Section IV-G explicitly state that per-frame detector invocation draws 70 W on Jetson AGX Thor.

claims.text: ALBIREO’s threshold sweep (u = 3 × 10^-4 to 1 × 10^-3) forms the upper Pareto frontier among the evaluated systems in the AP@50 ≥ 0.50 operating region on both Jetson platforms.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO’s threshold sweep ( u = 3 × 10 -4 to 1 × 10 -3 ) forms the upper Pareto frontier among the evaluated systems in the AP@50 ≥ 0 . 50 operating region on both Jetson platforms.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Sweeping the primary uncertainty threshold on YOLO26x traces an AP@50–EDP Pareto frontier that dominates the evaluated frame-skipping baselines (FixedSkip-N, CTD, Statues) within the target operating region (AP@50 ≥ 0.50).
claims.reason: Section IV-B and Figure 2 confirm that ALBIREO's threshold sweep forms the upper Pareto frontier in the AP@50 ≥ 0.50 region on both platforms.

claims.text: ALBIREO reduces energy by 12.1-17.6% while keeping AP@50 within 1.2 pp of per-frame inference.
claims.poster_quote: ALBIREO reduces energy by 12.1-17.6% while keeping AP@50 within 1.2 pp of per-frame inference.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Across all evaluated detectors and platforms, ALBIREO keeps AP@50 within 1.2 pp of Vanilla per-frame inference while reducing energy by 12.1–17.6%.
claims.reason: Section I and Table IV confirm the energy reduction range and AP@50 consistency across detectors and platforms.

claims.text: Per-clip power traces (Total, GPU, CPU, IO/MEM) are shown for two representative BDD100K clips on Thor with YOLO26x.
claims.poster_quote: Fig. 7. Per-clip power traces (Total, GPU, CPU, IO/MEM) for two representative BDD100K clips on Thor with YOLO26x.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Figure 7 highlights the two operating modes on representative clips. On a dense urban clip (no empty frames; 96% AI rate), ALBIREO and Vanilla draw similar power because the detector runs on most frames; rescue primarily preserves AP@50 rather than reducing energy. On a sparse highway clip (69% E, 4% AI), ALBIREO’s GPU power drops sharply during long ERD-only stretches, while Vanilla continues running full detector inference.
claims.reason: Figure 7 explicitly shows per-clip power traces for two representative BDD100K clips on Thor with YOLO26x.

claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On a dense urban clip (no empty frames; 96% AI rate), ALBIREO and Vanilla draw similar power because the detector runs on most frames; rescue primarily preserves AP@50 rather than reducing energy.
claims.reason: Figure 7 and Section IV-H describe dense urban traffic with 0% E and 96% AI, where rescue preserves AP@50.

claims.text: In sparse highway (69% E, 4% AI), long ERD-only stretches sharply reduce GPU power.
claims.poster_quote: Right: sparse highway ( 69% E, 4% AI), where long ERD-only stretches sharply reduce GPU power.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On a sparse highway clip (69% E, 4% AI), ALBIREO’s GPU power drops sharply during long ERD-only stretches, while Vanilla continues running full detector inference.
claims.reason: Figure 7 and Section IV-H describe sparse highway scenes with 69% E and 4% AI, where GPU power drops during ERD-only stretches.

claims.text: Frame-state transitions across consecutive frames are shown, with edges representing events that move execution between ERD skipping, prediction-only, normal inference, and rescue-augmented inference states.
claims.poster_quote: Fig. 1. Frame-state transitions across consecutive frames. Edges show the events that move execution between ERD skipping, prediction-only, normal inference, and rescue-augmented inference states.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Figure 1 illustrates how execution moves between these states across consecutive frames as scenes become empty or non-empty, uncertainty triggers fire, detections match, or rescue is needed.
claims.reason: Figure 1 explicitly shows frame-state transitions across consecutive frames, with edges representing events.

claims.text: AI follows the same next-frame routing as I; self-loops are omitted.
claims.poster_quote: AI follows the same nextframe routing as I; self-loops are omitted.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: AI follows the same next-frame routing as I; self-loops are omitted.
claims.reason: Section III-D and Figure 1 confirm that AI follows the same next-frame routing as I, with self-loops omitted.

claims.text: Default ALBIREO relative to vanilla across detectors and platforms shows values as changes from per-frame inference, averaged over 200 BDD100K MOT validation clips.
claims.poster_quote: DEFAULT ALBIREO RELATIVE TO VANILLA ACROSS DETECTORS AND PLATFORMS. VALUES ARE CHANGES FROM PER-FRAME INFERENCE, AVERAGED OVER 200 BDD100K MOT VALIDATION CLIPS.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Table IV evaluates ALBIREO’s detector-agnostic design across three off-the-shelf detectors and two Jetson platforms. Across the evaluated detectors, AP@50 remains within ±1.2 pp of Vanilla while energy savings range from 12.1% on RF-DETR-Large/Orin to 17.6% on YOLO26x/Thor.
